32:When no built-in adapter for a type exists and no custom adapter has been registered, Gson falls back to using reflection to access the fields of a class (including `private` ones). Most likely you are seeing this error because you (by accident) rely on the reflection-based adapter for third-party classes. That should be avoided because you make yourself dependent on the implementation details of these classes which could change at any point. For the JDK it is also not possible anymore to access internal fields using reflection starting with JDK 17, see [JEP 403](https://openjdk.org/jeps/403).

part.text:
Implemented in `gson/src/main/java/com/google/gson/GsonBuilder.java`:

- `registerTypeAdapter` now rejects `Object`, `JsonElement`, and any `JsonElement` subclass with `IllegalArgumentException("Cannot override built-in adapter for " + type)`.
- `registerTypeHierarchyAdapter` now rejects `JsonElement` and its subclasses while still allowing `Object`.
- Updated both method Javadocs, including the `@JsonAdapter` workaround.

Validated with `mvn -pl gson test` in `/testbed`; all tests passed.
